briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will begin the climate briefing for August 28, 2026. Today, we will examine the globally intensifying threat of climate change and various domestic and international efforts to address it.

sections.title: 🔴 Nepal Floods and Himalayan Glacier Collapse: A Direct Warning of the Climate Crisis
sections.content: In Nepal, large-scale floods and landslides have occurred, with 469 confirmed deaths and over 1,400 missing persons, including reported South Korean nationals [2, 103, 105]. This catastrophe was caused by the melting of glaciers and permafrost in the Himalayan region, serving as direct evidence that climate change is destabilizing the 'Roof of the World' [7, 9, 13, 15, 20, 21, 27, 106, 144]. Experts warn that this incident, where a glacier collapse the size of '25 football fields' led to massive floods, could be the prelude to a 'chain of disasters' caused by the climate crisis, with support from the international community and domestic rescue teams continuing [15, 27, 30, 104, 146]. This demonstrates climate change's counterattack, surpassing previous disaster predictions, such as floods occurring even without rain [9].

sections.title: ⚠️ Intensification of El Niño Phenomenon: Acceleration of Global Climate Pattern Changes
sections.content: Currently, the 'Super El Niño' phenomenon is strengthening, with consecutive research findings indicating that climate change is intensifying the frequency and strength of El Niño [3, 5, 108, 109, 128, 141]. According to research on Galapagos coral fossils, El Niño has become 36% stronger and super-intensified due to global warming [118, 121, 124, 130, 142]. This amplification of the El Niño phenomenon is accelerated by the burning of fossil fuels, leading to global climate pattern changes and causing extreme weather events such as heatwaves [19, 145]. This clearly demonstrates the impact of anthropogenic climate change, extending beyond purely natural phenomena [108].

sections.title: 🌍 Widespread Global Impacts Due to Climate Change: Increased Vulnerability of Ecosystems and Humanity
sections.content: Climate change is affecting not only Nepal's floods and the intensification of El Niño but also various regions worldwide in diverse ways. Ghana's World Heritage castles are collapsing due to climate change, with projections that they will be destroyed within 40 years [4, 29]. A sharp rise in sea surface temperatures is exacerbating the malnutrition crisis among children in low-income countries, and research also indicates that 580 million children worldwide will be exposed to an additional 20 days of 'heatwave stress' annually due to climate change [32, 120, 122, 134]. Furthermore, widespread damage to ecosystems is being reported, including reduced early rainy season rainfall in Puerto Rico and Jamaica, impacts on trout and salmon populations in UK rivers, and a decrease in fish stocks off Daecheongdo Island in South Korea [17, 111, 125].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic and International Carbon Neutrality Practices and Policy Trends
sections.content: Efforts to achieve carbon neutrality in response to the climate crisis are actively underway both domestically and internationally. Gangjin County plans to invest 96.5 billion KRW to construct the Byeongyeongcheon Dam in response to climate change [1]. Various local governments, including Anseong City and Nowon-gu, are establishing public-private cooperation systems through the launch of carbon neutrality committees and citizen declarations [36, 37, 55, 57]. Corporations are also participating in carbon neutrality activities; Harim is carrying out low-carbon home meal missions with the Pio Volunteer Group, and Hanyuwon is encouraging the accumulation of carbon neutrality points by introducing unmanned PET bottle collection machines [39, 42, 61, 64]. Meanwhile, alongside the carbon neutrality declaration by global battery company CATL, domestic policy challenges and discussions continue, including renewed criticism that the passage of the carbon neutrality act amendment 'postponed the climate crisis to the future' and constitutional debates [43, 44, 67, 79].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Infrastructure Expansion Efforts
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is a core pillar of climate crisis response, and efforts to improve related systems and expand infrastructure are accelerating. The Ministry of Climate launched a 'Direct PPA Brokerage Platform' to enable RE100 companies to easily purchase renewable energy, achieving the success of signing a 210MW power contract as its first agreement [84, 87, 89, 92]. Minister Kim Sung-hwan of the Ministry of Climate visited the Sihwa and Hwaong districts to inspect large-scale solar power deployment and announced plans to develop them into renewable energy hubs for the Seoul Metropolitan Area, accelerating project implementation [83, 90, 94, 98, 100]. Revisions to renewable energy-related systems, including biogas and wind power, have also begun, with the restructuring of the energy transition regulatory framework gaining momentum [80]; however, there are also calls for additional efforts, such as utilizing ESS (Energy Storage Systems) and electric vehicles, to solve power storage issues arising from the expansion of solar and wind power [95].

briefing.closing: Through today's climate briefing, we have confirmed the severity of climate change and the various domestic and international efforts to address it. We must continue climate action and policy support to create a sustainable environment for future generations. This concludes today's climate briefing.
